wiring.aria-modal: true on the content part only while modal is true, because that is the only state in which the family makes the background inert. The APG warns that a dialog marked modal without the background actually being inert has severe consequences for the readers who rely on the mark
wiring.aria-labelledby: the content names its title part; a consumer who writes their own aria-label instead keeps it, and no title part is rendered
wiring.aria-describedby: the content names its description part when a description part is present. The modal dialog pattern makes it optional and advises omitting it for structured content, which is what scroll=viewport holds
wiring.aria-haspopup: dialog on the trigger of both members
wiring.aria-expanded: true on the trigger while the layer is open
wiring.aria-controls: the trigger names the content part
wiring.aria-busy: true on the body while the family is loading
wiring.role: dialog on the content part, alertdialog for the alert member

keyboard.effect: moves to the next tabbable element inside the layer, and wraps from the last to the first while modal
keyboard.focus: the next tabbable element inside the layer

keyboard.effect: moves to the previous tabbable element inside the layer, and wraps from the first to the last while modal
keyboard.focus: the previous tabbable element inside the layer

keyboard.effect: asks the topmost layer to close, carrying the reason escape; a layer that refuses stops the request reaching the layer beneath it, so one Escape never closes two
keyboard.focus: returns to the element that held it when the layer opened

back.mechanism: one entry of the session history per modal layer, held by @slotted/core/dismissable-layer: pushed on the same URL over the state that was there when the layer opens, and taken back when the layer closes by any other path. A popstate that leaves the entry is the platform's way back — a phone's gesture, a browser's button — and it asks the topmost layer holding an entry to close with the reason back; a layer that refuses puts its entry back, so the page under it stays where it was
back.modalOnly: a non-modal layer holds no entry: the page stays reachable under it, and the way back is the page's
back.reason: On a phone the way back is the one gesture every reader knows, and a modal layer that leaves the page open behind it while the history moves under it is the defect the Nexora demo met first with the command palette. Android's own dialogs, Material's bottom sheets and every native sheet answer the gesture; the browser's history is the only way a web page hears it

focus.contain: while modal, from @slotted/core/focus. A non-modal layer contains nothing, because a non-modal dialog is reachable from the page by definition
focus.initial: the first tabbable element, the content itself, or an element the consumer names
focus.restore: the element that held focus when the layer opened, or its nearest connected ancestor when that element has since left the document
focus.reason: The two capabilities docs/component-features.md section 3 asks of packages/core/src/focus and it did not have. They arrive with the first consumer, not with dismissable-layer, which answers whether a layer should still be open

result.reason: What the platform calls returnValue and Angular Material returns from afterClosed(). It rides on the close request rather than declaring a second state model: nothing about a result is controlled, there is no initial one, and a consumer owning it would own a value only the family can produce

anatomy.root: the layer: fixed to the viewport, the query container, and a one-cell grid the backdrop and the viewport are both placed in
anatomy.backdrop: the scrim, in that one cell
anatomy.viewport: the other element in that cell: the box that centers the panel and, under scroll=viewport, the box that scrolls. It is separate from the root because a scrim inside a scrolling box scrolls away with it, and a scrim outside one cannot be a cell of the same grid
anatomy.content: the panel: a three-row grid, auto minmax(0, 1fr) auto; the body takes row 2 and the footer row 3, so a panel without a body or without a header keeps its footer on the last row

container.name: slotted-dialog
container.reason: The layer is the query container and the panel is the descendant it sizes, which is the split docs/build-briefing.md records. The breakpoint is a literal because @container (min-width: var(--x)) is invalid: a container condition cannot hold a custom property

scroll.content: the body scrolls; the header and the footer stay
scroll.viewport: the whole panel scrolls inside the layer, for content that is a document rather than a task
scroll.reason: The content part is a three-row grid, auto minmax(0, 1fr) auto, inside a bounded block size. Radix and React Aria ship no layout at all, so a long body pushes the footer past the fold and the reader cannot reach Save — which is what the default exists to prevent

mount.active: the layer exists only while it is open, and @slotted/core/presence holds it through its own exit; a layer mounted open enters from its closed style, and onOpenChangeComplete (React) / openChangeComplete (Angular) reports true when the entrance has ended and false when the exit has, so a layer rendered conditionally is removed after its exit
mount.lazy: the layer is built on the first open and kept afterwards
mount.eager: the layer exists from the start and is hidden while closed
mount.reason: The default is the opposite of collapsible's, and for the same reason: a disclosure's panel transitions its own height and needs to be in the DOM, while a layer transitions opacity and a transform that presence already keeps mounted. A layer left in the DOM holds its controls in the page tab sequence, which is the defect eager exists to be chosen deliberately

fullScreen.never: the panel keeps its margins and its measure at every width
fullScreen.narrow: below the container breakpoint the panel fills the layer and loses its radius and its margins
fullScreen.always: the panel fills the layer at every width
fullScreen.reason: docs/component-features.md section 8 asks that a dialog be able to take the screen on mobile, and section 2.7 asks that the responsive mode be testable deterministically. A container query is; a pointer: coarse query is not

open.result: the value of the close, cancel or action part that was pressed

dialogElement.reason: The platform ships the top layer, ::backdrop, browser-enforced tab containment, browser-enforced inertness, Escape as a cancellable cancel event and returnValue, and none of the six surveyed libraries uses any of it. What decides it here is the top layer itself: an element promoted to it paints above every element in the document regardless of z-index, and every other overlay in this library is portalled to the end of the body and stacked with --slotted-z-index-overlay plus --slotted-layer-depth. A select opened inside a dialog would portal to the body and paint behind the dialog it belongs to, with no z-index able to correct it
dialogElement.alsoCosts: closedby, the only declarative light dismiss, is not yet Baseline; ::backdrop is a pseudo-element, so the scrim could not be a data-part a consumer replaces; and animating in and out needs @starting-style, overlay and transition-behavior: allow-discrete, where @slotted/core/presence already completes an exit whose animation event never arrives
dialogElement.cost: The family depends on JavaScript for containment, inertness and Escape, where the platform supplies all three; a page with scripting disabled has no dialog at all; and this library maintains a focus trap that browsers already implement
dialogElement.revisitWhen: the library's overlay set moves to the top layer as a whole, which is one decision for packages/core and not one for this family

dialogService.reason: Angular Material's MatDialog.open(Component) returning a MatDialogRef with afterClosed() exists because Angular had no block control flow and no lazily rendered standalone component when it was designed. With @if and signals the same thing is three lines in the consumer's own template, afterClosed() is the closed output carrying the same result, closeAll() is the consumer's own signal, and data injection is the component's own inputs, checked by the compiler rather than cast from a token
dialogService.cost: Opening a dialog from a service with no template in scope is not possible, and the imperative handle does not recover it. It is written on the Angular reference page

scrollStrategy.reason: Angular Material offers block, reposition, close and noop. A dialog is anchored to the viewport rather than to an element, so reposition describes nothing; closing on scroll is a tooltip and popover policy; noop is modal=false, which is already an axis. block is the only one that applies, and it is what the scroll lock does

scrollCue.reason: A rule under the header drawn only while the body is actually scrolled needs scroll-state() container queries, which are limited availability — the same ground on which collapsible declined interpolate-size. The header and footer rules are drawn unconditionally instead, and the cost is a rule under a header that has nothing above it to separate

dragAndResize.reason: docs/component-features.md section 8 gives a modeless movable window its own Specialized family in wave 8. A modal dialog that can be dragged is a floating window with a scrim

edgePlacement.reason: docs/process/build-order.md wave 5 item 4. Base UI's own usage guideline says the same: a panel needing gestures or snap points is Drawer, not Dialog

positioner.reason: A dialog is anchored to the viewport, not to an element, so there is nothing to position against and no collision to resolve. @slotted/core/positioner is not composed

liveAnnouncer.reason: The dialog role announces the layer itself, and a second announcement would be the same message twice

header.free: the words column, under the description
header.reason: The header is a three-column grid and the family places four parts in it. Anything else a consumer writes there — a badge beside the title, a breadcrumb, a second line — used to auto-place into whichever cell was free, which is column one when no icon is rendered. Every unplaced child now lands in the words column instead, under the description, so where it goes is a rule rather than an accident of the grid.

surface.panel: the family paints the panel: surface, border, radius, shadow, and the three rows that keep the footer on screen
surface.plain: the family paints nothing at all — no background, no border, no radius, no shadow, no rows and no padding — and the consumer supplies the box. The panel stays at full opacity and its children fade in its place, because in Chromium an ancestor below full opacity draws no backdrop filter inside it: a material the consumer draws blurs from the first frame of the entrance to the last of the exit
surface.keeps: plain keeps the whole mechanism: the portal, the scrim, presence, focus containment and restoration, the dismissal policy and the single z-index stack
surface.reason: render substitutes the element the panel is drawn on and not the drawing, so a consumer who wanted the layer without the picture — a media viewer, an image at its own aspect ratio, a card of their own — had no way to say so. It is an axis rather than a second family because everything but the paint is identical, and it is the one place this library differs from a headless one: Radix and Base UI ship no panel at all, so plain is what their Content already is.
